**Needs changes before merge.**

Tier: SAFETY (new geometry code: cut sides and material release on a sheet). The PR does not change posted G-code or goldens.

### What looks good

- The parent #2808 is merged. The PR has one commit on top of main. The trial merge with `upstream/main` (`2ec4ad7e0`) is clean and touches only the 6 PR files.
- The code has no `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` outside tests. The indexing is safe: each node has the minimum vertex count before `segments()` and `points[0]` are used.
- The integer math is safe. Coordinates are below `COORD_LIMIT * SCALE` (1e18), so `cross` and `dot` fit `i128`. The area sum uses `checked_add` and refuses an overflow by name.
- The containment check refuses crossing and touching boundaries before the containment probe. Thus one probe vertex is enough.
- The release walk in `validate::order` checks each ancestor. It refuses a cut after the material is free.
- The corner formula `r * (1 / sin(θ/2) - 1)` is correct for a tool that touches the two edges.
- The new files have provenance lines. All files are below 400 lines. The test file is in the geometry crate, and its Gate map names `camcraft_geometry::nesting::cut_order`. The decision file is present. There is no new dependency.
- The body has `Changelog:` and ends with `Fixes #2159`.

### Results (locally)

**Not built.** The shared `sccache` server on this machine stopped. Each `rustc` call stays at the first crates (`cfg-if`, `memchr`). This occurs for all worktrees on the machine, not only for this review. I tried 3 builds for a total of more than 40 minutes:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run`: stopped at the xtask build.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test nesting_cut_order`: stopped at `memchr`.

I give no pass for the suite, clippy or the quick gate. Thus I did not run the mutations again. The author's results (17 pins, 21 mutations, clippy) are not verified by this review.

Extra suites run: none were due. The diff changes no `testdata/` file and no importer code.

### Requested before merge

1. **`Auto` side is wrong inside a closed contour that does not cut through** - `crates/geometry/src/nesting/cut_order.rs:119` and `:138`, with `crates/geometry/src/nesting/cut_order/geometry.rs:188-195`.
   The role and the `Auto` side come from the depth parity. The depth counts each closed ancestor. A closed contour with `release_phase: None` (a `Marking` engraving, or a blind pocket) does not separate material. But it still adds one level of depth.
   Example (from reading the code):
   - Part `1`: rectangle 0..20, `Breakthrough`, release `Breakthrough`.
   - Engraving `2`: rectangle 2..18, passes `[Marking]`, release `None`.
   - Through hole `3`: rectangle 5..8, `Breakthrough`, release `Breakthrough`, side `Auto`.

   The parent of `3` is `2` (the smallest closed contour that contains it). Thus `3` gets depth 2, role `PartOutline` and side `Outside`. The correct result is `Hole` and `Inside`. When an adapter uses this side, the kerf goes on the wrong side and the hole is too large by the cut width. The corner diagnostics of `3` also use the wrong side.
   A blind pocket with a through hole in its floor (a counterbore) has the same problem.
   Fix: count only ancestors that release material (`release_phase.is_some()`) for the role and the `Auto` side. Or refuse an `Auto` side when a non-releasing closed contour is an ancestor. Add a pin for the two cases (engraving and blind pocket). Do a mutation check on that pin.

### Notes (not blocking)

- `crates/geometry/src/nesting/cut_order.rs:26` says "Breakthrough is always a through cut on a closed contour". But `validate::requests` accepts an open chain with a `Breakthrough` pass. Refuse it, or change the comment.
- `geometry::forest` compares all segment pairs of all closed pairs. A large sheet (for example 100 parts with 200 vertices each) does about 10^8 segment tests. A bounding-box test for each feature pair before the segment loop makes this much faster.
- After the fix, please run the quick gate again. I will build it when the compile cache on this machine works again.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: Incorrect role and Auto side for a through hole inside a non-releasing engraving or blind pocket.

Depth now counts only ancestors that release material. Geometric parent links remain unchanged.

Pins:
- `through_hole_inside_engraving_uses_material_depth`
- `through_hole_inside_blind_pocket_uses_material_depth`

Both tests check the parent, depth, Hole role, Inside side, and corner diagnostics. Both fail with the original code and pass with the fix.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed: 938 steps, zero failures. Geometry selected the batch fallback. Clippy passed for the geometry crate with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.

New head: `ff18a784dd2f5f80c15a25c21fd02097a37bd85f`.

Please re-review this head.

Needs changes before merge: required heavy validation is incomplete.

Tier: SAFETY. This PR adds geometry rules for cut sides and material release. It changes no posted G-code or goldens.

What looks good:

- The earlier cut-side finding is resolved. Depth counts only ancestors that release material. Geometric parents remain available for scheduling.
- Both new tests check the parent, depth, Hole role, Inside side, and corner diagnostics.
- The trial merge with `upstream/main` at `11402dba4c849c5f827dccebc14f850196614311` is clean.
- The seven changed files add no dependency, importer, UI change, or fixture. The decision entry explains the policy.
- I found no new source defect. The numeric bounds, checked area sum, geometry refusals, and release checks remain in place.

Results, locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-2847`:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test nesting_cut_order --test nesting_cut_order_retained_stock`: 19 passed, zero failed. The restored code passed all 19 again.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed. I used a separate artifact directory inside the review worktree.
- Quick gate: incomplete. Geometry and kernel test builds passed. The CL build waited on an artifact lock. The interrupted gate later advanced to the app build. There is no complete green result.
- Heavy plan: 235 steps. The diff reaches every motion and app heavy target.
- Heavy release build: passed in 35 minutes. The following `motion heavy: lib` step waited on a build lock. The run reached its 40-minute limit with exit 124. No heavy test verdict is available.
- Interrupted commands left child processes and caused lock contention during this review. This is a review execution problem, not evidence of a source defect.
- Light lane: not run. Pixel snapshots and physical machine execution: not run.

Extra suites run: none were due. The diff changes no test data, fixture, golden, or importer code.

Mutations, run by this reviewer:

1. Count all closed ancestors, including retained stock. Both retained-stock tests failed with depth 2 instead of 1.
2. Replace checked area accumulation with wrapping accumulation. `sheet_refuses_area_accumulation_overflow_by_name` failed because the planner accepted the overflow.

Both mutations failed at runtime, not during compilation. After restoration, all 19 tests passed. No mutation remains in the worktree.

Requested before merge:

1. `crates/geometry/src/nesting.rs:4`: complete the reached heavy lanes on this head. Run `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`. Record the motion and app results in the PR body. Current upstream AGENTS.md requires green results for reached heavy lanes before readiness. The body states that heavy lanes were not run, and this review did not complete them. Also complete the quick gate and light lane before the next readiness check.

No golden files moved, so no golden comparison was due. No screenshot was due because the PR changes no UI.

The label remains `needs-rework`. The draft remains a draft because this review is not clean.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
